history.summary: Sri Sri Radha Banke Bihari Temple, popularly ISKCON Patna, is the first ISKCON temple in Bihar and, by campus area, the largest Hindu temple in Patna (reportedly the fourth-largest ISKCON temple in India). The foundation stone was laid in April 2007 by then Chief Minister Nitish Kumar (one official tourism source says 1984 - conflict flagged); construction commenced in 2010 at a reported cost of about Rs 100 crore, developed in phases. The first phase was inaugurated on 3 May 2022 (Akshaya Tritiya) by Nitish Kumar and Governor Phagu Chauhan after prana pratishtha, with the complex completed in 2023. The 108-foot, 84-pillared multi-storey temple at Golok Dham, Buddh Marg stands on a 2-3 acre campus with guest house, restaurant, auditorium and youth programmes. Note: the 'ISKCON Boring Road Base' is a separate nearby preaching centre, not this temple.

name: ISKCON Temple Patna
town_description: Patna, the capital of Bihar on the southern bank of the Ganges, is among the world's oldest continuously inhabited cities - the ancient Pataliputra, capital of the Mauryan and Gupta empires. The ISKCON temple stands at Golok Dham on Buddh Marg in Adalatganj, in the central Veerchand Patel Road area, about 2 km from Patna Junction. Patna today is a major administrative, educational and religious centre with a 2011 population of about 1.7 million.

travel.airport: Jay Prakash Narayan International Airport, Patna, approx. 6 km; taxis and app cabs available.
travel.railway: Patna Junction approx. 2 km; auto-rickshaws and city buses on Buddh Marg.
travel.road: Golok Dham, Buddh Marg, Adalatganj, Veerchand Patel Road area, Patna 800001; well connected by city buses, autos and taxis.

visitor_information.best_time: All year round. Janmashtami and the annual Jagannath Ratha Yatra are the most vibrant events, drawing large crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 4:30 AM to 9:00 PM daily per the temple's official listing; one source gives segmented timings (4:30 AM-5 PM, 7:30 AM-1 PM, 4:30 PM-8:45 PM) - verify. Morning aarti at 4:30 AM. Mobiles/cameras allowed; remove footwear and maintain decorum.
